checks: The complement of a finite family of closed caps is an open convex intersection. Its trace T has conv(T) inside the same intersection, hence T=P intersect conv(T), even if its affine span is proper and even if the whole zero set is not closed.

Failure at each positive site supplies a containing cap of mass strictly less than M/k; the whole-base trace cannot be such a cap. The finite covering constraints on positive sites are intersections of finite unions of closed threshold conditions. The threshold box is compact and feasible at the initial thresholds.

At a maximizing threshold vector, any nonsaturated coordinate has an exclusive equality witness. Otherwise the finite set of positive sites relying only on that coordinate either is empty or has a positive minimum slack, so that coordinate could increase. Saturated caps are empty on all P; hence at least one nonsaturated cap exists and they cover exactly P outside T in union.

A same-parity witness pair has a midpoint in P by lattice completeness, strictly below every active threshold by the exclusive equality patterns, and positive by midpoint concavity. The same holds for a witness and a point of T in its parity class, using h=0 on T and h>0 at the witness. Thus r+k(T)<=k without assuming that U and the whole zero set have disjoint parities.

The sum of the r cap weights is strictly below r M/k and bounds M-V(T) from above. The empty trace would give M<M; the nonempty proper trace violates its nonstrict quota. If h is everywhere positive, only the empty-trace branch is needed.

For a lower-rank minor with direction space W, the inherited lattice has direction lattice L intersect W. On differences within W, belonging to 2L is equivalent to belonging to 2(L intersect W), since the half-difference lies in W. Closed base halfspaces in a larger ambient space induce either relative halfspaces or the whole trace. The singleton rank-zero case has depth M.

Verified original 27d482de82ed9f88 §3, (7) and maximal-threshold argument against its committed source bytes. The source initially assumes sampled concavity, then explicitly notes that midpoint concavity alone is used; the frozen formulation accurately extracts that weaker hypothesis and keeps the original total mass and quota.

overlap.comparison: The weighted midpoint-label center result covers the case with h positive on all sites. It does not constrain the selected center to U in the presence of zero values; applying it on U alone replaces M by V(U) and omits the zero-site cap masses.

Its midpoint-closed lattice graph Helly proof also uses exclusive witnesses, but supplies an unrestricted graph center at the ambient parity budget. It does not charge the disjoint classes in a surviving zero-set minor and does not give the claimed original-mass positive-site selector.

It proves strict parity budgets for proper closed minors of an attained smallest bad canonical base; that can supply quotas in a separate application. It neither selects a positive h site nor replaces the midpoint-concavity argument here.

readability: The word closed for T refers to the closed-minor condition, although T is the trace of an open convex set. The proof's last sentence means restriction to the inherited lattice on the affine span of T, not to the possibly nonsaturated subgroup generated by its site differences.
review_method: Independent mathematical proof review of the frozen normalized candidate
summary: The maximal-threshold argument proves the weighted occupied-parity bound at a positive h site using only midpoint concavity and quotas on closed minors inside the zero set.
